title: Policy on the Handling of Complaints

articles.heading: Purpose and Scope
paragraphs: The purpose of this policy is to establish the procedure for handling complaints regarding the services or staff representing the Cible Retour à l'Emploi corporation, hereinafter referred to as "the corporation."

It is based on the corporation's commitment to offering job search assistance services, access to the facilities available at our offices, and up-to-date information about the Montreal job market, meeting the quality and diligence standards required for the best possible efficiency and effectiveness. It constitutes a fair and transparent process that respects human rights and is based on the values embraced by the corporation's members: respect, empathy, responsibility, and collaboration. It is shared with participants, the board of directors, staff members, and the public through our website at: www.cibleretour.com.

articles.heading: Person Designated to Handle Complaints
paragraphs: The executive management is responsible for applying this policy and complaint-handling procedure. It may designate another staff member, and an alternate, for receiving and handling complaints.

articles.heading: Definition of a Complaint
paragraphs: A complaint is the written or verbal expression of dissatisfaction by a participant or citizen requesting our services regarding the reception received, the service(s) offered, the delivery of the service(s) received, communications, or any other element that may negatively affect the job search process undertaken during service delivery by the corporation.

articles.heading: Subjects of a Complaint
paragraphs: A complaint may concern one of the following subjects: the quality of the services received; the respect and courtesy shown; the availability of staff, trainees, or other representatives of the corporation; a breach of confidentiality of information obtained in the course of duties by a staff member, trainee, or other representative of the corporation; serious harm or wrongdoing caused by a staff member, trainee, or other representative; any breach or violation of a law in force in Quebec affecting a participant's rights; the unjustified refusal by a staff member to provide assistance and a listening ear to a participant or citizen requesting our services.

articles.heading: Complaint Concerning Executive Management or the Designated Person
paragraphs: Executive management handles any complaint concerning the person designated for complaint handling. If it is deemed preferable for executive management to refrain from handling a complaint, for example when the complaint concerns executive management itself, the complaint will then be handled by the chair of the board of directors, who acts as the alternate. Any complaint concerning executive management must be addressed to the chair of the board of directors.

chapters.heading: Chapter 2 – Filing and Receiving the Complaint

articles.heading: Filing a Complaint
paragraphs: Any current, former, or future participant, or their assign, may file a written or verbal complaint with the designated person or their alternate, if applicable, concerning one or more of the subjects listed in point 4 of this policy.

articles.heading: Referral of a Complaint
paragraphs: Any employee, trainee, or representative of the corporation who receives a complainant must immediately refer them to the person responsible for handling complaints and provide them with the corporation's complaint form. This form is also available on the corporation's website.

articles.heading: Content of a Written Complaint
paragraphs: A written complaint must contain the following elements: the date of the complaint; the complainant's name and address; the subject of the complaint; the identification of the people concerned; a brief statement of facts; the goals being pursued.

articles.heading: Receiving the Complaint
paragraphs: The person designated to handle complaints must assist the complainant in formulating their complaint and provide them with all information relating to the application of the complaint-handling procedure. They must record the subject of the complaint using the complaint receipt form, read this document to the complainant, and have them approve its content.

articles.heading: Notice of Receipt
paragraphs: Within five (5) business days of receiving a complaint, the designated person sends the complainant written notice indicating the date the complaint was received and their commitment to handle the complaint within 90 days of its receipt.

articles.heading: Admissibility of the Complaint
paragraphs: The person designated to handle complaints, after reviewing the content of the complaint, determines whether it is admissible or not. A complaint is not admissible, among other reasons, if it does not fall within the corporation's jurisdiction, or if it is frivolous or vexatious. If the subject of the complaint does not fall within the corporation's jurisdiction, the designated person notifies the complainant and informs them, if applicable, of the possible jurisdiction of another recipient. If the complaint is deemed inadmissible, the designated person informs the complainant in writing and files a copy of their decision in the administrative complaint file.

articles.heading: Conciliation
paragraphs: The designated person handling a complaint must assess the merits of the complaint and, taking into account the facts and circumstances that gave rise to it, propose to the people concerned any solution likely to improve customer satisfaction and respect for their rights. They may make any recommendation they deem appropriate.

articles.heading: Investigation
paragraphs: The designated person may summon any person to a meeting and ask them to provide any information they deem useful for analyzing the complaint. If this person is a staff member, trainee, or other representative of the corporation, they are required to comply with the summons. After gathering all information from other sources, they must hear the account of the person named in the complaint.

articles.heading: Consultations
paragraphs: The designated person, with the authorization of the board of directors regarding related expenses, may consult any person whose expertise they deem useful for handling the complaint.

articles.heading: Case Analysis
paragraphs: The person designated to handle complaints must determine whether the complaint is well-founded or not, and may enlist the assistance of a person such as the chair of the board of directors or another board member for this purpose.

articles.heading: Conclusions
paragraphs: The designated person must document their decision and implement the corrective measures necessary to remedy the situation.

articles.heading: Review of Disciplinary Matters
paragraphs: When a practice or the behaviour of the person named in the complaint raises disciplinary questions, the designated person must refer the matter to executive management, if applicable, for evaluation and decision. Executive management must then diligently review the matter. The designated person must be informed of the outcome of the disciplinary matter and, if applicable, of any disciplinary action taken against the person named in the complaint. At the request of executive management, the board of directors must rule on any matter that could lead to a sanction: suspension, dismissal, or other measure.

articles.heading: Response to the Complainant
paragraphs: The designated person must communicate their conclusions to the complainant, inform them whether their complaint was found to be well-founded or unfounded, and, if applicable, inform them of the corrective measures that were applied.

articles.heading: Expiry of the Investigation Period
paragraphs: If the designated person has not completed their investigation within 90 days of receiving the complaint, they must, upon expiry of this period, inform the complainant in writing and report on the progress of the investigation. As long as the investigation is not complete, the designated person must, every 90 days after the expiry of the period, inform the complainant in writing and report on the progress of the investigation.

articles.heading: Intervention
paragraphs: The designated person may intervene on their own initiative when facts come to their attention and they have reasonable grounds to believe that the rights of a participant or citizen are not being respected or that a breach has occurred.

articles.heading: Creation of the Complaint File
paragraphs: The complaint file is created and maintained by the person designated to handle complaints. This file is confidential and is only accessible to people who, by virtue of their duties, participate in handling the complaint and the decision, and these people are bound to respect confidentiality.

articles.heading: Content of the Complaint File
paragraphs: The complaint file must contain any document or correspondence relating to the complaint and its handling, produced or received by the designated person.

articles.heading: Prohibition
paragraphs: No document included in the complaint file may be placed in a staff member's file, except for the designated person's decision and the disciplinary notice, if applicable.

articles.heading: Retention of Documents
paragraphs: After it is closed, the complaint file is kept for six (6) years. At the end of this period, the designated person ensures its destruction.

articles.heading: Protection
paragraphs: When the person who is the subject of the complaint is informed that an investigation is taking place, they are prohibited from communicating with the complainant without the prior written permission of the designated person.

articles.heading: Retaliation
paragraphs: The designated person and the board of directors, as applicable, must intervene in whatever manner they deem most appropriate and without delay when they are informed that a person who has filed a complaint or intends to file a complaint is being subjected to retaliation of any kind.

articles.heading: Entry into Force
paragraphs: This policy comes into force upon its adoption by the board of directors.

articles.heading: Review
paragraphs: The complaint-handling policy and procedure is periodically reviewed at intervals not exceeding three (3) years.
